zif-socket.context: A zero insertion force chip socket with a grid of pin holes and its locking lever raised. Used on chip programmers, test benches and older processor boards where chips are swapped often.

toroidal-inductor.context: A ring shaped ferrite core wrapped with turns of copper wire, with two leads below. Found in power supplies, filters and switching regulators on circuit boards.

ferrite-bead.context: A short ferrite tube threaded on a single wire. Used on circuit boards and leads to suppress high frequency noise and interference.

ferrite-choke.context: A clip-on ferrite choke made of two halves clamped around a cable. Snapped onto power, data and video cables to cut radio frequency interference.

seven-segment-display.context: A display showing a figure eight built from seven bar segments plus a decimal point. Used for numbers on clocks, meters, counters and appliance panels.

led-matrix.context: A square board covered in a grid of round LEDs. Used to show scrolling text, symbols and simple pixel graphics in signs and maker projects.

character-lcd.context: A wide LCD module showing two rows of text characters, with header pins along the top edge. A common text display for microcontroller and hobby electronics projects.

oled-display-module.context: A small breakout board with a dark square OLED screen and four pins along its top edge. Used as a tiny graphic screen in sensors, wearables and hobby projects.

e-paper-display.context: A thin e-paper panel showing lines of text, with a flat ribbon cable at the bottom. Used in e-readers, shelf labels and low power signs that keep their image without power.

led-bar-graph.context: A rectangular LED bar graph block with a row of vertical light segments. Shows levels such as volume, signal strength or battery charge on panels and meters.

rgb-led.context: A domed LED with four legs of different lengths, one for each colour channel and a common lead. Used for colour changing lights, status indicators and mood lighting.

addressable-led-ring.context: A ring shaped circuit board carrying a circle of small square LED chips that can each be set to any colour. Used for light rings, clocks, status halos and wearables.

laser-diode-module.context: A small cylindrical laser module with a lens at the front, two power wires at the back and a beam leaving the lens. Used in pointers, level tools, sensors and hobby projects.

photoresistor.context: A light dependent resistor: a small round disc with a winding track across its face and two legs. Its resistance drops in bright light, so it is used in night lights and light sensors.

nixie-tube.context: A tall glass nixie tube with a glowing numeral inside and pins at its base. Used as retro number displays in clocks, counters and vintage instruments.

piezo-disc.context: A thin round piezo disc: a brass plate with a smaller ceramic disc on top and two wires soldered on. Used as a contact microphone, knock sensor or simple sounder.

piezo-buzzer.context: A short cylindrical buzzer with a sound hole on top and two legs. Beeps in alarms, timers, appliances and circuit boards to signal an event.

electret-microphone.context: A small round electret microphone capsule with a mesh face and two pins. Found inside phones, headsets, recorders and sound sensor boards.

vibration-motor.context: A flat coin shaped vibration motor with two thin wires, shown with buzz marks. Gives haptic feedback in phones, watches, controllers and wearables.

gear-motor.context: A small cylindrical DC motor joined to a gearbox with an output shaft. Drives wheels, robots, toys and slow moving mechanisms that need more torque.

linear-actuator.context: An electric linear actuator: a motor housing at one end of a long tube with a push rod coming out the other. Lifts desks, opens hatches and moves parts in a straight line.

peltier-module.context: A thermoelectric cooler shown from the side: two ceramic plates with a row of pellets between them and two wires. One side gets cold while the other gets hot, used in mini fridges and chip coolers.

case-fan.context: A square computer case fan with screw holes in the corners, a round hub and curved blades. Moves air through PC cases, servers and equipment enclosures to keep parts cool.

solid-state-relay.context: A solid state relay block with four screw terminals and an indicator light. Switches mains loads such as heaters and lamps silently from a small control signal.

contactor.context: An electrical contactor with rows of screw terminals along the top and bottom and a window in the middle. Switches motors, pumps and heavy loads in control panels.

toroidal-transformer.context: A thick donut shaped toroidal transformer with a mounting bolt through the centre and wires coming out. Used in audio amplifiers and power supplies for its low hum.

lipo-battery.context: A flat lithium polymer pouch cell with two wires leading to a small plug. Powers drones, remote control models, phones and portable gadgets.

battery-holder.context: A plastic battery holder tray with two cylindrical cells side by side and two wires out of the end. Powers toys, remotes and hobby projects from standard cells.

battery-snap.context: A nine volt battery snap: a small cap with one round and one hexagonal stud and two wires. Clips onto a 9V battery to power smoke alarms, pedals and hobby circuits.

battery-tester.context: A battery tester with a needle dial above a slot that holds a cell. Checks how much charge is left in household batteries before use.

buck-converter.context: A small DC to DC converter board with a round coil in the middle and screw terminals at each end. Steps a higher voltage down to a lower one for chargers and projects.

voltage-regulator.context: A three legged voltage regulator with a metal tab, a mounting hole and a V label. Holds a circuit at a steady supply voltage on power boards and adapters.

bridge-rectifier.context: A square bridge rectifier block with four legs and AC, plus and minus marks on top. Turns alternating current into direct current in power supplies and chargers.

capacitor-bank.context: A row of three tall capacitors joined by a bus bar across their tops. Stores energy or corrects power factor in power supplies, inverters and electrical plant.

busbar.context: A flat metal bus bar with a row of evenly spaced bolt holes. Carries heavy current and shares power or earth connections inside switchboards and battery packs.

din-rail.context: A length of top hat DIN rail with slotted mounting holes along its centre. Holds breakers, relays and terminal blocks in control panels and fuse boards.

slip-ring.context: A slip ring: a cylinder with stacked contact rings and wires out of each end. Passes power and signals across a rotating joint in turntables, cameras and wind turbines.

rheostat.context: A wire wound rheostat: a coil of resistance wire with a sliding contact on a bar above it. Adjusts current by hand in labs, motor speed controls and old dimmers.

decade-resistance-box.context: A decade resistance box with a row of dials on its lid and two terminals on top. Sets an exact resistance by hand when testing and calibrating circuits.

heating-cartridge.context: A cartridge heater: a short metal rod with two wires out of one end and heat waves above it. Heats 3D printer hot ends, molds and metal blocks.

tube-socket.context: A vacuum tube socket with a ring of pin holes, a centre key and mounting ears. Holds valves in guitar amplifiers, hi-fi amps and vintage radios.

shield-can.context: A small metal shield can with vent holes, soldered onto a circuit board. Covers radio and processor sections of phones and routers to block interference.

slot-optical-sensor.context: A U shaped slotted optical sensor with a gap between two uprights and legs below. Detects when something passes through the slot, as in encoders, printers and end stops.

female-header.context: A female pin header: a strip with a row of square sockets on top and pins below. Takes jumper wires and plug-in boards on development and prototyping boards.

jumper-cap.context: A small jumper cap bridging two pins on a header strip. Sets options and configurations on circuit boards, hard drives and motherboards.

wire-to-board-connector.context: A small keyed plastic plug with a latch on top and a row of wires entering its back. Links batteries, fans, sensors and speakers to circuit boards.

banana-plug.context: A banana plug with a grip body, a cable and a sprung pin tip. Used on test leads, lab power supplies and speaker wires.

bnc-connector.context: A BNC plug with a bayonet collar and its locking slot, a body and a cable. Connects oscilloscopes, test gear, CCTV cameras and RF equipment.

test-hook-clip.context: A test hook clip: a pen shaped grabber with a thin wire hook out of its tip. Grips component legs and chip pins during testing and measurement.

spade-terminal.context: A crimp spade terminal with a forked tip, a barrel and a wire. Fits under screw terminals on switches, terminal blocks and car wiring.

butt-splice-connector.context: A butt splice connector: a short tube with a wire entering each end, crimped in the middle. Joins two wires end to end in car, marine and household wiring.

bullet-connector.context: A pair of male and female bullet crimp connectors about to join. Used for quick disconnects on motors, batteries, speakers and car wiring.

circular-connector.context: A round multi-pin connector face with a key and a threaded coupling ring. Used in aviation, military, industrial and outdoor equipment where plugs must lock tight.

micro-usb-connector.context: A micro USB plug with a small trapezoid metal tip, a grip and a short cable. Charges and connects older phones, power banks and small gadgets.

usb-type-b-connector.context: A USB type B plug with a square metal tip with bevelled top corners and a cable. Connects printers, scanners, audio interfaces and some lab gear to a computer.

usb-type-a-connector.context: A USB type A plug with a flat rectangular metal tip, two square holes and a cable. The standard plug for computer ports, chargers, keyboards and flash drives.

fiber-optic-connector.context: A square fibre optic plug with a thin ferrule tip, a boot and a cable. Joins optical fibres in network racks, patch panels and broadband installations.

keystone-jack.context: A snap-in keystone jack module with a network port on its face and wire slots on top. Clips into wall plates and patch panels to terminate network cable.

pcie-slot.context: A long PCI Express expansion slot with a short and a long section and a latch at one end. Holds graphics cards and other add-in cards on a motherboard.

dimm-slot.context: A long memory slot with a key notch and clips at both ends. Holds RAM sticks on computer motherboards.

twisted-pair-cable.context: Two insulated wires twisted around each other in a regular helix. Twisting cuts interference, so pairs like this carry data in network and phone cables.

coiled-cable.context: A cable wound into a tight spring coil between two plugs. Stretches and springs back, as on phone handsets, keyboards and workshop tools.

y-splitter-cable.context: A Y splitter cable with one plug whose cable divides into two branches, each ending in a plug. Shares one output between two devices, such as headphones or fans.

heat-shrink-tubing.context: A piece of heat shrink tube over a wire joint with heat waves rising above it. Shrinks tight when heated to insulate and protect soldered or crimped joints.

braided-cable-sleeve.context: A braided sleeve with a woven crosshatch pattern covering a bundle of wires. Tidies and protects cables in PCs, cars and home offices.

cable-ferrule.context: A wire end ferrule: a metal tube with a plastic collar crimped onto the end of a stranded wire. Keeps strands together in screw terminals and push-in terminals.

cable-harness.context: A wiring harness: a tied bundle of wires that branches out to three connectors. Routes power and signals through cars, machines and appliances.

cable-comb.context: A cable comb plate with wires passing straight through its holes. Keeps wires parallel and neat when dressing cable bundles in racks and panels.

wire-marker.context: A printed wire marker sleeve with a number, slipped over a wire. Labels wires so each one can be identified in panels, looms and installations.

ground-strap.context: A flat braided ground strap with a ring terminal at each end. Bonds engines, chassis, doors and equipment racks to earth.

grounding-clamp.context: A ground clamp fixed around a pipe, with a wire running from its bolt to an earth symbol. Connects plumbing and metal work to the earthing system of a building.

cable-tester.context: A network cable tester made of a main unit and a remote, each with a jack and a row of lights. Checks that every wire in a network or phone cable is connected correctly.
